sections.overview: Pinguipes brasilianus is a marine sandperch in the family Pinguipedidae, native to the southwestern Atlantic.
sections.identification: It is a demersal fish associated with rocky reef communities in northern Patagonia.
sections.habitat: Its reported range extends along the southwestern Atlantic coast from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, to Golfo Nuevo, Argentina.
sections.diet: A Patagonian reef study found a narrow, specialized diet consisting mainly of reef animals such as sea urchins, limpets, bivalves, crabs and polychaete worms.
sections.behavior: Field studies describe it among demersal fishes associated with shelter on rocky reefs; details of its daily activity remain poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: In northern Patagonian waters, spawning extends across spring and summer, with reproductive activity peaking around late spring and summer.
sections.ecology: Its specialized reef diet relies strongly on local prey, and the species is recorded as native in Argentina.
sections.conservation: The Argentine national inventory lists it as not evaluated; this is a local assessment record, not evidence of a global Red List category.
